---
title: "Prerequisites"
---

::: {.ao-story}
Before the road, the quartermaster checks your pack. A traveller without a lantern turns back at the first tunnel. Check each item once, now, and the installs are done.
:::

This page lists what to install for the hands-on exercises. Reading is separate: see [Read first](read-first.html). Nothing here needs real data. Exercises use invented files unless the page says otherwise.

## Required

| Tool | Check it works | Needed for |
|---|---|---|
| A terminal | open it and type `echo hello` | every exercise |
| Python 3 | `python3 --version` | the database exercise and the analysis exercises |
| git | `git --version` | the undo and change-history exercises |
| Claude Code | `claude --version` | every exercise that runs an agent |

- **Terminal.** macOS: Terminal. Linux: any terminal. Windows: a WSL 2 (Windows Subsystem for Linux) terminal, because the exercises assume a Linux-style shell and the sandbox needs it.
- **Claude Code install.** The first agent quest gives the installer command. Read an installer script before piping it into `bash`.
- **An account.** Claude Code needs a login on a paid Claude plan, or an Anthropic API key (a secret string that gives programmatic access, billed per use). Use the account your organisation approves.
- **WSL 2 on Windows.** Follow Microsoft's WSL install page, then open the Ubuntu terminal.

## Optional

| Tool | Check it works | Needed for |
|---|---|---|
| Docker | `docker --version` | the optional container exercise |
| Ollama | `ollama --version` | running a model on your own computer |
| OpenCode | `opencode --version` | an open-source agent, if you prefer one |
| bubblewrap and socat | `bwrap --version` | the sandbox exercise on Linux and WSL 2 (two helper tools) |

Claude Code is the agent the exercises use. Nothing in the course asks you to use an LLM.

## A first check

Run this once from any folder. Each tool should print a version number:

```bash
python3 --version && git --version && claude --version
```

## If something fails

- `command not found`: the program is not installed, or its folder is not on your `PATH` (the list of folders the shell searches for programs).
- If the shell cannot find `claude`, add its folder to `PATH`: `export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"` in `~/.bashrc` or `~/.zshrc`, then open a new terminal.
- On a managed laptop, ask your administrator before installing.
- Do not run the exercises on a cluster login node (the shared machine you log in to first).
